newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges up on futures, some shortage.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges up on futures, some shortage.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges rose on Wednesday on Tuesday's futures gains and perceived shortages, traders said.
High sulphur cargoes fetched steady to stronger numbers but pressure was looming with avails seen.
High sulphur barges traded late in the afternoon at $88 fob ARA, after earlier trades at that level or 50 cents higher, compared with Tuesday's close of $87, the high for that day.

"Crude futures rose sharply last night and prompt supplies are tight, and so the market was higher today. The herd mentality took over, with some buying higher and others following suit," one trader said.
Antwerp traders said a major was having a logistics problem and can only supply material from July 24 onwards and a refiner was short of material and was not selling into the market at the moment.

"In Rotterdam there is also little product after July 21-22 and refinery product is a little bit more expensive...In combination with the higher NYMEX, of course people were paying $88/$88.50," one trader said.
"If there was much more demand we would have seen $89/$89.50," he added.
Low sulphur barges were steady, with 1,700 tonnes changing hands at $95 fob, the same as a deal late last week. The seller started at $96 but moved down later with little other demand seen.
Russian high sulphur cracked fetched steady to stronger prices on one deal but with avails seen in the market and demand waning a little, other sellers cut their price a little.

A Russian trader sold an M-40 out of Klaipeda to a trader, and traders said that the 27,000-tonne loader had a price tag of two means +$1.75 for cracked and two means +$6 if it was straight-run. This was unchanged to a touch firmer than Tuesday's levels.
"The market is still holding steady, basically on crude going up and on good demand," one trader said.
But other traders said that two other cracked M-100 cargoes were being offered a little lower, at two means +$0.75/$1.
One percent was said to be steady at $93.50/$94 a tonne for fob cargoes, with some buyers on the market eyeing the possibility of shipments trans-Atlantic.
A 45,000-tonne cargo was heard sold at $102.35 cif to a buyer in the Mediterranean, a little higher than last done.
